# dlarrj

> Refines eigenvalue approximations of a symmetric tridiagonal matrix using bisection given initial intervals.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlarrj from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlarrj';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlarrj(
    N,
    d, strideD,
    E2, strideE2,
    ifirst, ilast, rtol, offset,
    w, strideW,
    WERR, strideWERR,
    WORK,
    IWORK,
    pivmin, spdiam
) → info: integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the tridiagonal matrix |
| `d` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Diagonal elements of T, length N |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride length for `d` |
| `E2` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N - 1</sub> | Squares of the subdiagonal elements of T, length N-1 |
| ↳ `strideE2` | `integer` | Stride length for `E2` |
| `ifirst` | `integer` | Index of the first eigenvalue to be computed (1-based) |
| `ilast` | `integer` | Index of the last eigenvalue to be computed (1-based) |
| `rtol` | `number` | Tolerance for convergence of bisection intervals |
| `offset` | `integer` | Offset for the arrays w and WERR |
| `w` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Eigenvalue approximations (in/out), length N |
| ↳ `strideW` | `integer` | Stride length for `w` |
| `WERR` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Error estimates for eigenvalues (in/out), length N |
| ↳ `strideWERR` | `integer` | Stride length for `WERR` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ 2 * N</sub> | **out** · Workspace array, length 2\*N |
| `IWORK` | `Int32Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ 2 * N</sub> | **out** · Integer workspace array, length 2\*N |
| `pivmin` | `number` | Minimum pivot in the Sturm sequence for T |
| `spdiam` | `number` | Spectral diameter of T |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The order of the matrix.
- `d`: The N diagonal elements of T.
- `E2`: The Squares of the (N-1) subdiagonal elements of T.
- `ifirst`: The index of the first eigenvalue to be computed.
- `ilast`: The index of the last eigenvalue to be computed.
- `rtol`: Tolerance for the convergence of the bisection intervals. An interval \[LEFT,RIGHT\] has converged if $\mathrm{RIGHT}-\mathrm{LEFT} < \mathrm{RTOL} \, \max (|\mathrm{LEFT}|,|\mathrm{RIGHT}|)$.
- `offset`: Offset for the arrays W and `WERR`, i.e., the `IFIRST`-`OFFSET` through `ILAST`-`OFFSET` elements of these arrays are to be used.
- `w`: On input, W( `IFIRST`-`OFFSET` ) through W( `ILAST`-`OFFSET` ) are estimates of the eigenvalues of L D L^T indexed `IFIRST` through `ILAST`. On output, these estimates are refined.
- `WERR`: On input, WERR( `IFIRST`-`OFFSET` ) through WERR( `ILAST`-`OFFSET` ) are the errors in the estimates of the corresponding elements in W. On output, these errors are refined.
- `WORK`: Workspace.
- `IWORK`: Workspace.
- `pivmin`: The minimum pivot in the Sturm sequence for T.
- `spdiam`: The spectral diameter of T.

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 on success

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlarrj.strided(
    N,
    d, strideD, offsetD,
    E2, strideE2, offsetE2,
    ifirst, ilast, rtol, offset,
    w, strideW, offsetW,
    WERR, strideWERR, offsetWERR,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork,
    IWORK, strideIWork, offsetIWork,
    pivmin, spdiam
) → integer
```

Refine eigenvalue approximations using bisection given initial intervals.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns |
| `d` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Input array |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride length for `d` |
| ↳ `offsetD` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `d` |
| `E2` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N - 1</sub> | Input array |
| ↳ `strideE2` | `integer` | Stride length for `E2` |
| ↳ `offsetE2` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `E2` |
| `ifirst` | `integer` | The index of the first eigenvalue to be computed. |
| `ilast` | `integer` | The index of the last eigenvalue to be computed. |
| `rtol` | `number` | Tolerance for the convergence of the bisection intervals. |
| `offset` | `integer` | Offset for the arrays W and WERR, i.e., the IFIRST-OFFSET through ILAST-OFFSET elements of these arrays are to be used. |
| `w` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideW` | `integer` | Stride length for `w` |
| ↳ `offsetW` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `w` |
| `WERR` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideWERR` | `integer` | Stride length for `WERR` |
| ↳ `offsetWERR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `WERR` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length ≥ 2 * N</sub> | **out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride length for `WORK` |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `WORK` |
| `IWORK` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length ≥ 2 * N</sub> | **out** · Output array |
| ↳ `strideIWork` | `integer` | Stride length for `IWORK` |
| ↳ `offsetIWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `IWORK` |
| `pivmin` | `number` | The minimum pivot in the Sturm sequence for T. |
| `spdiam` | `number` | The spectral diameter of T. |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The order of the matrix.
- `d`: The N diagonal elements of T.
- `E2`: The Squares of the (N-1) subdiagonal elements of T.
- `ifirst`: The index of the first eigenvalue to be computed.
- `ilast`: The index of the last eigenvalue to be computed.
- `rtol`: Tolerance for the convergence of the bisection intervals. An interval \[LEFT,RIGHT\] has converged if $\mathrm{RIGHT}-\mathrm{LEFT} < \mathrm{RTOL} \, \max (|\mathrm{LEFT}|,|\mathrm{RIGHT}|)$.
- `offset`: Offset for the arrays W and `WERR`, i.e., the `IFIRST`-`OFFSET` through `ILAST`-`OFFSET` elements of these arrays are to be used.
- `w`: On input, W( `IFIRST`-`OFFSET` ) through W( `ILAST`-`OFFSET` ) are estimates of the eigenvalues of L D L^T indexed `IFIRST` through `ILAST`. On output, these estimates are refined.
- `WERR`: On input, WERR( `IFIRST`-`OFFSET` ) through WERR( `ILAST`-`OFFSET` ) are the errors in the estimates of the corresponding elements in W. On output, these errors are refined.
- `WORK`: Workspace.
- `IWORK`: Workspace.
- `pivmin`: The minimum pivot in the Sturm sequence for T.
- `spdiam`: The spectral diameter of T.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `RangeError` `IWORK` must have at least `2 * N` elements from `offsetIWork`

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N <= 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

Error flag.

</section>

## Notes

-   `dlarrj()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLARRJ`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlarrj.f).

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import dlarrj from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlarrj';

// Refine the eigenvalues of T = tridiag( 1, 2, 1 ), which are 2 - sqrt(2), 2, 2 + sqrt(2):
const N = 3;
const d = new Float64Array( [ 2.0, 2.0, 2.0 ] );
const E2 = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 1.0 ] );
const PIVMIN = 2.2250738585072014e-308;
const SPDIAM = 4.0;
let w = new Float64Array( [ 0.6, 2.0, 3.4 ] );
let WERR = new Float64Array( [ 0.1, 0.1, 0.1 ] );
const WORK = new Float64Array( 2 * N );
const IWORK = new Int32Array( 2 * N );

// Using the standard interface:
let info = dlarrj( N, d, 1, E2, 1, 1, N, 1.0e-14, 0, w, 1, WERR, 1, WORK, IWORK, PIVMIN, SPDIAM );
console.log( info, w, WERR ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

// Using the strided interface:
w = new Float64Array( [ 0.6, 2.0, 3.4 ] );
WERR = new Float64Array( [ 0.1, 0.1, 0.1 ] );
info = dlarrj.strided( N, d, 1, 0, E2, 1, 0, 1, N, 1.0e-14, 0, w, 1, 0, WERR, 1, 0, WORK, 1, 0, IWORK, 1, 0, PIVMIN, SPDIAM );
console.log( info, w, WERR ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLARRJ`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

Given the initial eigenvalue approximations of T, DLARRJ does bisection to refine the eigenvalues of T, W( `IFIRST`-`OFFSET` ) through W( `ILAST`-`OFFSET` ), to more accuracy. Initial guesses for these eigenvalues are input in W, the corresponding estimate of the error in these guesses in `WERR`. During bisection, intervals \[left, right\] are maintained by storing their mid-points and semi-widths in the arrays W and `WERR` respectively.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
